summary: This is Snowflake's reference page for the PARSE_IP function, which returns a JSON object with the components of a valid INET or CIDR IPv4 or IPv6 string. It describes the syntax, the required type and optional permissive arguments, the always-returned and version-specific JSON elements, and includes examples for subnet range lookups with IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. The page's navigation menus and footer are boilerplate and were ignored.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the PARSE_IP function, which parses INET or CIDR IPv4/IPv6 strings into a JSON object with subnet range details.
key_facts: PARSE_IP returns a JSON object consisting of all the components from a valid INET or CIDR IPv4 or IPv6 string.
The type argument supports either INET or CIDR and its value is case-insensitive.
If the permissive flag is set to 0, parse errors cause the function to fail; the default value is 0.
If the permissive flag is set to 1, parse errors result in an object with the error field set to the error message and no other fields set.
The always-returned elements are family, ip_type, host, and ip_fields.
The family element is 4 for IPv4 or 6 for IPv6.
The ip_fields element is an array of 4 numeric fields, each between 0 and 4,294,967,295 (2^32 - 1), inclusive.
For IPv4 addresses, the ipv4 element is the numeric IP address matching the first field in ip_fields.
When a subnet mask is included, the results include network_prefix_length, a numeric value identifying the length of the subnet mask.
For IPv6 addresses, hex_ipv6 expresses the IP address as a fully padded, fixed-size hexadecimal value.
Snowflake recommends storing PARSE_IP output in a VARIANT column when inputting a subnet mask for better performance.
The snowflake$type element is reserved for internal Snowflake usage.
In the IPv4 example, '192.168.242.188/24' produces ipv4_range_start 3232297472 and ipv4_range_end 3232297727.
